test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The title of 'Chief of the Merchants' or 'Malikut-Tujjar' was conferred on Mahmud Gawan by which of the following Bahamani kings?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Humayun Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humayun Shah** was one of the notable rulers of the **Bahamani Sultanate**, which ruled parts of the Deccan region in South India from the 14th to the 16th centuries.
 
• During his reign, **Mahmud Gawan**, a renowned administrator and scholar, served as his prime minister and made significant contributions to the administration and military of the Bahamani kingdom.
 
• The title of '**Malikut-Tujjar**' or '**Chief of the Merchants**' was conferred upon **Mahmud Gawan** by Humayun Shah as a recognition of his administrative acumen and his efforts in enhancing trade and commerce within the kingdom.
 
• **Mahmud Gawan** played a pivotal role in strengthening the economy of the Bahamani Sultanate by reforming the revenue system and promoting trade relations.
 
• He was instrumental in consolidating the Bahamani empire and extending its influence across the Deccan region.
 
• Humayun Shah’s reign is marked by significant administrative and military achievements, largely credited to the efforts of **Mahmud Gawan**.
 
• The Bahamani kingdom under Humayun Shah became a prominent power in the Deccan, with **Mahmud Gawan** being a key figure in its governance and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Mohammad Shah**__

 __
 
• **Mohammad Shah** was another ruler of the Bahamani Sultanate, but he is not associated with conferring the title of '**Malikut-Tujjar**' to Mahmud Gawan.
 
• His reign saw significant political challenges and conflicts within the Bahamani Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Nizamuddin Ahmad III**__
 __
 
• **Nizamuddin Ahmad III**, another Bahamani ruler, is not linked with Mahmud Gawan’s title or contributions.
 
• His rule is considered less impactful in comparison to Humayun Shah’s reign.
 
 
 
• **Bahman Shah**__
 
 
• **Bahman Shah** was the founder of the Bahamani Sultanate, established in 1347.
 
• Although he laid the foundation of the kingdom, the title '**Malikut-Tujjar**' was conferred much later during the reign of Humayun Shah.
